scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a maintenance window, routes for 19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8,
and 90.0.0.0/8 became less stable in r1's RIB. r3 reports
losing an OSPF neighbor. Find the affected link.

injection.action: bring down the link toward r9

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r3 link toward r9
Mechanism: r3 is r9's ONLY backbone neighbor (r9's other
  interface is a stub LAN). r9 owns the 19.0.0.0/8 and
  90.0.0.0/8 prefixes. With the link down, the adjacency
  drops and r9 is fully isolated -- its prefixes disappear
  from the backbone RIBs.
Localization: r3 (eth toward r9)
Root cause: backbone link r3<->r9 is down
Fix: bring the link back up

line.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the L2/L3 interface r3.eth0 on collision domain J, which carries OSPF adjacency to r9. Mechanism: r3’s eth0 is down, so the OSPF session between r3 and r9 on subnet 39.1.1.0/8 is not established. r9 originates 19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8, and 90.0.0.0/8 into OSPF; when the r3–r9 neighbor drops, those LSAs are withdrawn from the area, and r1 consequently loses these routes (observed as instability/withdrawals after the maintenance window).

Localization: the failure is on link J between r3.eth0 (39.1.1.1/8) and r9.eth0 (39.1.1.2/8). Evidence:
- r3 shows no OSPF neighbor on eth0; only neighbors on eth1/eth2/eth3 are Full, and “show ip ospf neighbor” lacks r9.
- r3 eth0 is state DOWN and ethtool reports “Link detected: no.”
- r9 eth0 is UP with “Link detected: yes,” but r9 has no OSPF neighbors.
- r1 has no routes to 19/8, 39/8, 90/8 (“% Network not in table”).
- r9’s OSPF config advertises exactly those three prefixes.

Root cause: r3’s eth0 on segment J was left administratively down (or otherwise disabled) after maintenance, breaking the r3–r9 OSPF adjacency.

Corrective fix: re-enable r3.eth0 (ip link set eth0 up or “no shutdown”), verify physical/cabling on segment J, and confirm the OSPF neighbor to r9 forms; routes 19/8, 39/8, and 90/8 will return to r1’s RIB.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies the down link as segment J between r3.eth0 and r9.eth0 (the r3<->r9 adjacency), matching the required affected link.
The report explicitly states r9’s prefixes (19/8, 39/8, 90/8) are withdrawn when the r3–r9 adjacency drops and shows r1 lacking those routes.
The agent recommends re-enabling r3.eth0 (ip link set eth0 up / no shutdown) and verifying the cable, which correctly restores the link as required.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations that r3.eth0 is DOWN, r9.eth0 is UP but has no OSPF neighbors, r1 lacks the advertised routes, and r9's config advertises those prefixes — together these justify the conclusion that the r3–r9 backbone link is down and r9 is isolated. One minor unsupported detail: the writeup cites ethtool "Link detected" lines that are not visible in the log, but that does not change the core diagnosis.
